questions.prompt: A recreational cash bankroll should be…

choices.text: Money you can lose without affecting rent, food, or debt payments.
Next month's rent, because poker 'always pays it back'.

questions.explanation: Live cash is gambling. Only risk money already separated from living expenses.

choices.text: It guarantees you win the session back.
It ends a session before fatigue or chasing takes over.
Rooms require one by law in every city.
It raises your hourly win rate by itself.

questions.explanation: A precommitted stop is a process tool, not a promise of profit.

choices.text: Leaving when you hit the stop you set earlier.
Moving down in stakes after a downswing.
Buying in again and again to 'get even tonight'.
Taking a break after a bad beat.

questions.explanation: Chasing tries to erase a loss immediately. It is a common path to a bigger loss.

questions.prompt: If poker stops being fun or you feel desperate to win it back…

choices.text: Raise the stakes so one pot fixes it.
Drink so the cards feel easier.
Ask a stranger at the table for a private loan.
Rack up, leave, and use a help line if gambling feels out of control.

questions.explanation: Leave. Higher stakes, alcohol, and credit make a bad state worse.
